title: The Last Choir Anew
premise: Isandro Winterbourne, gatekeeper of a sealed door beneath the city of Vellharrow, has spent twenty years posing as a charm-seller in a kingdom where magic is outlawed. When a child named Wren arrives at his shop speaking the First Tongue, Isandro learns her soul was sold to the Undercourt, the fae realm beneath the mountain, and that his own long-ago bargain — the one that sealed the gate and cost him his true name — is the reason she could be taken. To save her, he must cross into the Undercourt, steal her soul back from the Court of Bells, and confront the archivist who holds his name. In the end, Isandro trades his own restored identity for Wren's freedom, returns nameless but not empty, and finds a new family in the foundlings and outcasts who choose to remember him.
about_author: Mirabel Iversen is the pen name of a former cathedral archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval liturgical music before turning to fantasy. They live in a coastal town where they still sing in a small choir and collect bells.

chapters.title: The Shop of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Introduces Isandro's charm-shop in Vellharrow and his careful, gray life of selling harmless trinkets while hiding the sealed gate in his cellar. A routine inspection by the Ministry of Order raises the stakes of discovery. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment, and the first crack in twenty years of silence.

chapters.title: A Knock in the First Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A mud-streaked child named Wren appears at the door at nightfall, speaking a language Isandro recognizes from the gate itself — the First Tongue. When she touches the cellar door, the wards flare for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant wonder; the past knocking louder than the Ministry ever could.

chapters.title: What the Wards Remember
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro interrogates the gate and finds a new mark burned into it: a soul-contract, freshly signed, bearing Wren's name. He realizes someone below knows the gate is weak — and knows about him. Emotional beat: guilt, as he understands his old bargain left the door ajar.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Sold Herself
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Flashback chapters begin: Wren, an orphan of the Ashmarket, was promised bread and safety by a veiled merchant who had her sign a paper she couldn't read. She wakes with no reflection and a bell-like hum in her chest. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only kindness she'd known.

chapters.title: The Ministry Comes Calling
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Inspector Sera Quillon, a sharp-eyed officer with her own buried history, returns with questions about a missing child and reports of 'resonance' near Isandro's street. He lies badly. She notices. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension and the first hint that Sera is not her Ministry's creature.

chapters.title: Bells Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The veiled merchant returns to collect her, and Wren flees through Ashmarket, learning her stolen soul is 'payable' at the Court of Bells under the mountain — and that the debt comes due at the Turning of the Year, eleven days away. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of a Kept Door
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro finally tells Wren the truth: twenty years ago he bargained with the Undercourt's archivist to seal the gate, paying with his true name — and the archivist, Vess, has been using the thin spot to harvest souls ever since. Emotional beat: confession as release; the found family begins with shared shame.

chapters.title: Thieves' Vigil
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Isandro recruits his few trusted irregulars: Oskit, a dwarven fence with a grudge against the Undercourt; Maren, a defrocked priestess who remembers the old rites; and Sera, who arrives not to arrest but to bargain. Emotional beat: the wary, tentative forming of a company.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Year
chapters.summary: POV Sera. On the longest night, the veil thins and the Ministry seals the city for the annual Rite of Order. Sera falsifies the registers to buy the company passage — committing her first true betrayal of the state. Emotional beat: conviction over loyalty, fear over faith.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The company descends through Isandro's gate into the Undercourt's borderlands — a country of inverted forests and rivers of remembered songs. The First Tongue, which Wren now speaks natively, is the only map that holds. Emotional beat: awe and homesickness for a world none of them knew.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: POV Wren. In a fae market where names and memories are currency, the company trades pieces of themselves for passage. Oskit sells a grievance, Maren a doubt, and Isandro is recognized by a bell-servant who whispers his lost name like a curse. Emotional beat: the cost of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Chorus of the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. The company is ambushed by the Hollow — soulless fae who were once debtors like Wren. Maren's rites hold them off, but Oskit is taken. Emotional beat: first true loss; the price of the journey stops being theoretical.

chapters.title: What Oskit Saw
chapters.summary: POV Oskit. Held in the Court of Bells' antechambers, Oskit learns Vess's plan: at the Turning, the Court will ring the Great Bell with a chorus of harvested souls and rewrite the border between worlds — with Vellharrow as the first payment. Emotional beat: a cynic choosing to hope, and to escape.

chapters.title: The Court of Bells
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Disguised as a debt-broker, Isandro enters the Court itself: a cathedral of suspended bells where the Undercourt's nobility trade in souls like vintage wine. He finds Wren's soul — a small silver flame — in Vess's archive, and Vess finds him. Emotional beat: recognition between old enemies; the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Vess offers Isandro a bargain: his true name back, restored, in exchange for Wren and the gate. Isandro refuses — and learns the darker truth: his name is the linchpin of the Great Bell's working. Without it, the Court cannot ring the border into being. Emotional beat: temptation and clarity; identity as the story's fulcrum.

chapters.title: Escape on the Ninth Bell
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The company flees the Court during the ninth bell's pealing, using Wren's First Tongue to unbind the archive's locks. They retrieve Wren's soul but lose Sera, who stays behind to hold the door — and is taken by the Court. Emotional beat: victory soured by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In a cell of ringing silence, Sera bargains with a minor bell-lord, learning the Court's one vulnerability: the Great Bell can only be rung by a chorus of willing souls — and willingness can be revoked. Emotional beat: a woman of law learning to break rules from the inside.

chapters.title: Ashmarket Rising
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Back in Vellharrow, the Turning approaches and the city's bells begin to hum in sympathy. Wren, carrying her own soul in a lantern, rallies the Ashmarket's orphans and outcasts — those the Court quietly harvested for generations. Emotional beat: the found family becomes an army of the overlooked.

chapters.title: The Gate Stands Open
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The Court's host marches on the gate, demanding the name that will finish the Great Bell. Isandro makes his counter-bargain with Vess before both courts: his name freely given — but only if every harvested soul, Wren's included, is freed and the gate sealed from both sides. Emotional beat: the price of survival, finally named and paid.

chapters.title: The Last Choir
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Climax. At the Turning, the Court attempts to ring the Bell with a coerced chorus; Wren and the freed souls answer instead with the First Tongue's oldest song — a choosing, not a debt. The Great Bell cracks. Vess's archive burns, and Isandro's name dissolves into the song, spent at last. Emotional beat: triumph through surrender; identity given, not taken.

chapters.title: A Nameless Man in a Loud City
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Aftermath. The gate is sealed and silent, the Ministry in disarray, and Isandro cannot remember who he was — but Sera, Wren, Maren, and the freed Oskit remember for him, telling him his own story like a bedtime tale. Emotional beat: grief braided with warmth; memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Shop of Small Mercies, Reopened
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Epilogue. A year on, the shop thrives under new sign-paint: Wren apprenticing, Sera visiting off-duty, Oskit cheating at cards in the back room. On the cellar door, a new ward blooms — not a lock, but a welcome, written in the First Tongue. Emotional beat: home is not a place you keep; it's a door you leave open for the right people.
